description: Granular effect on incoming audio: the sound is written to a four second buffer and grains are cut from a position in it, moved by a built-in LFO or by CV

params.text: Sets how long each grain is, from 1 to 6400 samples
Attenuates the WINDOW CV, from nothing through to its full range
Sets where in the buffer grains are cut from, its start to its end, and while a cable is in the position input the LFO is not used
Attenuates the position CV, from nothing through to its full range
Sets how fast each grain reads through the buffer, -1.3 to 2 buffer samples per audio sample: 1 is the recorded speed, 0 holds one point, and below zero the grain is read backwards
Attenuates the PITCH CV, from nothing through to its full range
Sets the output level, from silence through unity at the centre to twice the level
Scatters the position each new grain is cut from, up to three thousand samples either way at the right
Chooses how the PAN input is read: bipolar -5V to 5V, or unipolar 0-10V
Stops new audio being written to the buffer, so the grains keep cutting the same four seconds
Sets how many grains may sound at once, up to 140
Attenuates the GRAINS CV, from nothing through to its full range
Sets how often a new grain is spawned, from one every 512 samples at the left to one per sample at the right
Attenuates the SPAWN RATE CV, from nothing through to its full range
Sets the speed of the LFO that moves the grain position
Attenuates the LFO frequency CV, from nothing through to its full range
Sets how far the LFO moves the grain position, from a hundredth of the buffer to all of it
Attenuates the LFO amplitude CV, from nothing through to its full range
Picks the LFO shape, through the five drawn on the panel
Attenuates the LFO waveform CV, from nothing through to its full range
Chooses whether the LFO output runs 0-10V or is centred on 0V

inputs.text: Multiplies the jitter spread by the voltage here, so 0V removes the scatter and 1V gives what the knob is set to
Adds to the grain length after its attenuator, -10V to 10V covering the full 1 to 6400 samples
Sets where in the buffer grains are cut from, 0-10V across the four seconds, in place of the LFO
Shifts the reading speed of each grain after its attenuator
A rising edge spawns one grain, and while a cable is patched here the spawn rate is not used
Places each new grain in the stereo field, left to right over the range the switch selects
Any voltage other than 0V stops new audio being written to the buffer, and the switch is then ignored
Adds to the grain count after its attenuator, 0-10V covering none to 140
The left channel of the audio written into the buffer
The right channel of the audio written into the buffer
Adds to the spawn rate after its attenuator, 0-10V covering its full range
Adds to the LFO speed after its attenuator, 0-10V covering its full range
Adds to the LFO depth after its attenuator, 0-10V covering its full range
Adds to the LFO waveform choice after its attenuator, 0-10V spanning the five shapes

outputs.text: The left channel of the grain cloud
The right channel of the grain cloud
The position the LFO has reached, in the range the polarity switch sets; it carries nothing while a cable is in the position input

notes: the buffer holds the last four seconds of incoming audio, and the lamp beside the outputs stays red until it has filled once
the outputs are silent until audio is patched into the inputs; the module makes no sound of its own

inputs.8:
